newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up, but off highs on report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up, but off highs on report.

text.p: The key March Euroyen contract on TIFFE ended higher on Monday in Tokyo, but bigger gains were pared on a U.S. news agency report that quoted a senior Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) official as saying a rise in Japan's official discount rate will probably be considered after the general elections, traders said on Monday.
The March rose to a high of 99.36, highest since December 22, in early trade in sympathy with the bullish bond market.
The March ended at 99.34, up from Friday's 99.31.

Shizuka Kamei, the Liberal Democratic Party's publicity chief, was quoted as saying that a rise in Japan's official discount rate, and other interest rates, will probably be considered after the October 20 general election.
Asked about the report, a Bank of Japan official said the central bank does not comment on such issues every time they emerge.
Kamei's reported remarks briefly pushed the March to a low of 99.32 before bargain-hunting emerged to help it recover by the close.
In the cash market, the overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.45 percent, up from the weighted average of 0.44 percent on Friday.
The rise in the key call rate reflected the market's caution over the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) market stance.

"The money market wanted to drive the call rate down below 0.40 percent in line with the fall in long-term yields, but traders instead drove it up a bit for fear that a steep call rate decline would trigger tight liquidity control by the central bank," said a senior money trader.

Many dealers said a fall in the call rate towards 0.40 percent would eventually induce a shift in the central bank's liquidity supply stance from neutral to tight. The BOJ conducted a neutral operation this morning.

There is almost a market consensus that the BOJ is reluctant to see interest rates falling too much from the current level and is ready to check what it sees as "excessive speculation" of easy credit.
A bank economist said that there seems to be some officials at the BOJ who believe the recent yen bond rally was overdone.
